source_user: Give one misleading intuition about tensor parallelism and correct it. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: A misleading intuition is that TP is simply free parallel speedup: splitting a layer across more devices must make every request faster. In reality, ranks compute shards and then wait for collectives such as all-reduce or all-gather, so synchronization and interconnect traffic can dominate when shards are small. TP can improve fit or reduce per-rank memory without reducing latency. Boundary: the result depends on layer shapes, TP degree, topology, batch, phase, and runtime; measure compute versus collective time and end-to-end latency before generalizing.
risks: TP speed and capacity effects are topology-, workload-, layout-, and runtime-specific.
A non-fitting or differently resourced baseline can invalidate a performance comparison.
evidence_required: Versioned model, layer shapes, precision, TP degree/layout, device topology, runtime, and matched baseline.
Replayed workload and protocol with per-rank memory, compute/collective/queueing telemetry, latency, throughput, and failures.
Repeated trials, uncertainty, and output/numerical correctness checks.

corrected_answer: It is misleading to assume that aggregate memory scales cleanly with the number of TP ranks. A sharded matmul reduces some local weights or activations, but replicated tensors, temporary buffers, padding, allocator fragmentation, and KV state can remain or concentrate on one rank. The mechanism is rank-local computation followed by a collective, not arbitrary pooling of HBM. Boundary: per-rank peak allocation determines fit, and a model can fit in aggregate yet OOM one rank. source_user: Give one misleading intuition about tensor parallelism and correct it. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: A common intuition is that more TP ranks always improve throughput because each rank does less arithmetic. Each rank instead also participates in synchronization and communicates partial results; if collective latency or imbalance exceeds the saved compute, throughput falls. Boundary: large batches may amortize this cost while small decode steps may be communication-bound, and capacity can improve even when speed does not. Hold workload, topology, precision, and kernels fixed, then measure phase-specific compute, collective, throughput, latency, and correctness.

source_user: Give one misleading intuition about tensor parallelism and correct it. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: The intuition that TP eliminates communication is backwards: sharding reduces local work but creates communication dependencies between ranks. A rank may finish its shard and wait for a collective before the next layer, so a faster local kernel need not lower end-to-end latency. Boundary: collective cost depends on tensor shapes, topology, rank placement, and runtime, while queueing can dominate serving tail latency. Trace a representative sharded operation and report collective time, rank imbalance, memory, latency percentiles, and throughput.
